definition_zh: n. 售货亭，摊位；（电话、投票等的）隔间
definition_en: a small structure for selling or showing goods; also a small enclosed space such as a phone booth or a voting booth
core_image: 集市上一排蓝白条纹的小亭子
scene: 集市那天，每个摊位只用一块帆布与邻摊隔开。At the fair, each booth was separated from the next by a single sheet of canvas.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：booth 指售货或展示用的小亭子；句意是集市上每个摊位只用一块帆布与邻摊隔开。

senses.title: A small stand for selling or showing
senses.definition: a small structure, often open at the front, where goods are sold or displayed
senses.definitionCN: 常正面敞开、用于出售或展示货物的小型结构
senses.example: She ran a coffee booth at the Saturday market.
senses.exampleCN: 她在周六集市上经营一个咖啡摊。
senses.why: The word first named a temporary hut, which is exactly what a fair stall is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指临时棚屋，而集市摊位正是如此。

senses.title: A small enclosed space for one purpose
senses.definition: a small enclosed area built for a single activity, such as telephoning or voting
senses.definitionCN: 为单一活动（如打电话或投票）而建的封闭小区域
senses.example: He called from a phone booth by the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站旁的电话亭里打电话。
senses.why: The selling sense fades and only the enclosed box remains.
senses.whyCN: 售货义淡去，只剩「封闭的小方盒」这层意思。

definition_zh: 使厌烦；钻孔；令人厌烦的人
definition_en: to make someone feel tired and uninterested
core_image: 听众在长讲座上打哈欠
scene: 那场讲座又长又闷，让人昏昏欲睡。The long lecture bored the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 bore 是「使厌烦」（第 1 个义项：让人感到无聊、提不起兴趣）；句意是那场长讲座让全班都感到乏味。

pos.zh: 名词：令人厌烦的人或事

senses.title: To make someone tired
senses.definition: to make someone feel tired because nothing interests them
senses.definitionCN: 因为毫无趣味而让人感到疲惫
senses.example: The long lecture bored the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 那场长讲座让全班都感到乏味。
senses.why: This is the everyday modern sense, though it came later than drilling.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代日常义项，但出现得比钻孔晚。

senses.title: To make a hole

senses.definitionCN: 在某物上钻出深的圆孔
senses.example: They bored a hole through the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在墙上钻了一个洞。

senses.title: A dull person

senses.example: He is a bore at parties.

senses.why: The verb became a noun for the person who causes the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，指引起这种感觉的人。

senses.title: A scientist who studies plants
senses.definition: a person who studies plants as a profession, usually with formal training in botany
senses.definitionCN: 以研究植物为职业的人，通常受过正式的植物学训练
senses.example: She became a botanist after finishing her doctorate on alpine mosses.
senses.exampleCN: 她完成关于高山苔藓的博士研究后成为植物学家。
senses.why: Botanist is botan- plus -ist, the agent suffix. The stem names the field and -ist names the person, so the word begins as 'one who practises botany' rather than as a description of a quality.
senses.whyCN: botanist 是 botan- 加施动后缀 -ist。词干命名领域，-ist 命名人，因此这个词的起点是“从事植物学的人”，而不是描述某种性质。

senses.title: Field botanist: the collector outdoors
senses.titleCN: 野外植物学家：在户外采集的人
senses.definition: a botanist who works in the field, finding, pressing, and recording plants where they grow
senses.definitionCN: 在野外工作的植物学家，在植物生长地寻找、压制并记录植物
senses.example: A field botanist spent three weeks surveying the valley's orchids.
senses.exampleCN: 一位野外植物学家花了三周调查这个山谷的兰科植物。
senses.why: The suffix identifies the person, while 'field' identifies where the practice happens. Collecting is the oldest form of the job: the specimen comes before the theory, so the agent noun is narrowed by its workplace.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标识人，field 标识实践发生的地点。采集是这份工作最古老的形式：标本先于理论，因此这个施动名词被工作场所所收窄。

senses.title: Taxonomist: the namer and classifier
senses.titleCN: 分类学家：命名与归类的人
senses.definition: a botanist who describes, names, and places plants in the taxonomic system
senses.definitionCN: 描述、命名并把植物放入分类系统的植物学家
senses.example: The botanist published a revision of the genus in a taxonomic journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这位植物学家在分类学期刊上发表了对该属的修订。
senses.why: Naming is the part of botany that turns a plant into a retrievable record. A taxonomic botanist is therefore the keeper of the Latin labels, a role rather than a new word.
senses.whyCN: 命名是把植物变成可检索记录的那部分植物学。因此分类植物学家就是拉丁标签的保管人；这是一种角色，而不是另一个新词。

senses.title: Specialist branches of the profession
senses.definition: a botanist may also be a plant physiologist, ecologist, geneticist, or molecular botanist, depending on the layer of the plant studied
senses.definitionCN: 植物学家也可以是植物生理学家、生态学家、遗传学家或分子植物学家，取决于研究植物的哪一层
senses.example: A molecular botanist studies the genes that control flowering time.
senses.exampleCN: 一位分子植物学家研究控制开花时间的基因。
senses.why: The same agent noun covers every subfield because all of them study plants. The modifier names the layer of study, not a different kind of person, so the core sense stays intact.
senses.whyCN: 同一个施动名词覆盖所有子领域，因为它们都在研究植物。修饰语命名的是研究层次，而不是另一种人，因此核心义保持不变。

senses.title: Historical: herbalist and plant collector
senses.titleCN: 历史义：草药师与植物采集者
senses.definition: before botany became a university science, a botanist was often a herbalist or an amateur collector of medicinal plants
senses.definitionCN: 在植物学成为大学科学之前，botanist 常指草药师或采集药用植物的业余爱好者
senses.example: In the 17th century a botanist might keep both a herb garden and a dried collection.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪，一位 botanist 可能既经营药草园，又保存干燥标本。
senses.why: The word is recorded from the 17th century, when plant knowledge was still tied to medicine. The modern professional sense grew out of that older practical role, so the agent noun widened before it narrowed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 17 世纪起有记录，当时植物知识仍与医药相连。现代的职业义正是从那更早的实用角色中长出来的：这个施动名词先变宽，后又收窄。

senses.title: Applied botanists outside academia
senses.titleCN: 学术界之外的应用植物学家
senses.definition: a botanist employed in agriculture, forestry, conservation, or industry, applying plant science to practical problems
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于农业、林业、保护或工业，把植物科学用于实际问题的植物学家
senses.example: An economic botanist searches for wild relatives of crop plants.
senses.exampleCN: 一位经济植物学家寻找农作物的野生近缘种。
senses.why: The suffix says what the person knows, not where they work. Applied fields therefore use the same noun and add a modifier for the sector, which is how the profession extends beyond the university.
senses.whyCN: 后缀说明这个人懂什么，而不是在哪里工作。因此应用领域用同一个名词，只添加标明行业的修饰语；职业范围就这样延伸到大学之外。

senses.title: Everyday: the knowledgeable plant lover
senses.titleCN: 日常用法：懂植物的爱好者
senses.definition: in informal use, a very knowledgeable plant enthusiast may be called a botanist, though not a professional one
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中，非常懂植物的爱好者也可被称为 botanist，但并非职业人士
senses.example: My neighbour is a botanist of sorts; she can name every weed in the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 我邻居算得上半个植物学家，巷子里每种野草她都叫得出名字。
senses.why: The word can be used loosely because the boundary of the profession is knowledge, not a licence. The hedge 'of sorts' keeps the informal use honest while borrowing the prestige of the agent noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以宽松使用，因为这一职业的边界是知识，而不是执照。of sorts 这样的限定语让非正式用法保持诚实，同时借用了这个施动名词的声望。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanist versus horticulturist
senses.definition: a botanist studies plants; a horticulturist grows and cultivates them for gardens, food, or sale
senses.definitionCN: botanist 研究植物；horticulturist 为园艺、食用或销售而栽培植物
senses.example: The botanist identified the species; the horticulturist worked out how to propagate it.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家鉴定了物种；园艺师则研究出如何繁殖它。
senses.why: Both work with plants, but one produces knowledge and the other produces plants. The suffixes differ as -ist of a science versus -ist of a cultivation practice, so the two agent nouns are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 两者都跟植物打交道，但一个产出知识，另一个产出植株。后缀同样都是 -ist，区别在于一个是科学，一个是栽培实践，因此两个施动名词不能互换。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanist versus biologist
senses.definition: a botanist is a kind of biologist; biologist is the wider term for anyone who studies living things
senses.definitionCN: botanist 是 biologist 的一种；biologist 是研究生物者的更宽泛称呼
senses.example: As a biologist she works on fungi; as a botanist she would have to exclude them.
senses.exampleCN: 作为生物学家她研究真菌；若作为植物学家，她就得把真菌排除在外。
senses.why: The stem restricts the field to plants, while -ist only marks the practitioner. Botanist is therefore narrower than biologist, not a synonym of it, because the stem does the restricting.
senses.whyCN: 词干把领域限制在植物，而 -ist 只标记从业者。因此 botanist 比 biologist 窄，不是它的同义词，收窄工作由词干完成。

intro.en: Botanist is the same stem as botany with a different suffix: botan- names the field and -ist names the person. The stem is Greek in origin and reached English through medieval Latin; the suffix is a general agent ending, not a plant word. The recorded dates for botanist and botany are slightly inconsistent, so the exact order of formation is uncertain.
intro.cn: botanist 与 botany 词干相同，后缀不同：botan- 命名领域，-ist 命名人。词干源自希腊语，经中世纪拉丁语进入英语；后缀是一般的施动者词尾，本身不是植物词。botanist 与 botany 的记录年代略有矛盾，因此确切的构词先后存疑。

items.en: Greek botanē meant 'plant, grass, pasture, fodder', and botanikos meant 'of herbs'. Etymonline notes that these words seem to have more to do with pasturage than with plant science; related forms include botamia 'pastures' and boter 'herdsman'. The deeper origin of the family is not established.
items.cn: 希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、草、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”。etymonline 指出这些词更多与放牧有关，而非与植物科学有关；相关形式有 botamia“牧场”、boter“牧人”。这个词族的更深来源尚未确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin botanicus 'of plants' carried the Greek adjective into learned Latin, and French botanique (17c.) passed the same stem into English as botanic.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 botanicus“植物的”把这个希腊形容词带入学术拉丁语，法语 botanique（17 世纪）又把同一词干以 botanic 的形式传入英语。

items.en: English botanic is recorded from the 1650s, botany from the 1690s, and botanist from the 1680s. Etymonline derives botany from botanic, adding -y on the model of astronomy, and botanist from botany + -ist. The dates leave botanist apparently earlier than botany; that contradiction means the exact derivation order is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 botanic 于 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，botany 于 17 世纪 90 年代有记录，botanist 于 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。etymonline 认为 botany 来自 botanic，仿 astronomy 加 -y；botanist 来自 botany + -ist。这些年代使 botanist 表面上早于 botany；这一矛盾说明确切的派生先后存疑。

items.en: -ist comes from Greek -istēs through Latin -ista and French -iste. It is built from the stem ending of verbs in -izein plus the agent suffix -tēs, and it forms nouns meaning 'one who practises or believes', as in artist, scientist, and botanist. It adds no plant meaning of its own.
items.cn: -ist 经拉丁语 -ista、法语 -iste 上溯希腊语 -istēs。它由 -izein 动词词干的结尾加施动后缀 -tēs 构成，形成表示“从事者或信奉者”的名词，如 artist、scientist、botanist。它本身不添加任何植物含义。

items.en: Herbaria, overseas expeditions, and Linnaean taxonomy turned plant study into a paid profession. Botanist then settled into its modern sense of a trained plant scientist, while the older overlap with herbalists and gardeners faded. The exact period of this shift is not fixed.
items.cn: 标本馆、海外考察与林奈分类学把植物研究变成有薪职业。botanist 由此固定为“受过训练的植物科学家”这一现代义，而与草药师、园艺者的旧重叠逐渐消退。这一转变的确切时期并无定论。

items.en: Modern usage adds modifiers for molecular, ecological, and conservation specialties but keeps one noun. The word stays narrower than biologist because its stem names plants, not life in general.
items.cn: 现代用法为分子、生态与保护等方向添加修饰语，却保留同一个名词。由于词干命名的是植物而非一切生命，这个词始终比 biologist 窄。

note.en: The first group is the same botan- stem with three different endings; the second separates the plant scientist from the gardener, the herbalist, the ecologist, and the wider life scientist.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 botan- 词干配三种不同后缀；第二组把植物学家与园艺者、草药师、生态学家及更宽泛的生命科学家区分开。

entries.definition: The science of plants. It is the field itself, while botanist is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的科学。它是学科本身，而 botanist 是从事这门学科的人。

entries.definition: Relating to plants or botany. It describes a quality or relation, while botanist names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 植物的；植物学的。它描述性质或关系，而 botanist 命名人。

entries.definition: In botanical terms; from the viewpoint of plant science. The -ly ending makes it modify a verb or statement, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 从植物学角度；以植物学的说法。-ly 结尾使它修饰动词或陈述，而不是人。

entries.definition: To collect or study plants in the field. The -ize suffix turns the field into an activity, so it names what a botanist does, not who they are.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外采集或研究植物。-ize 后缀把学科变成活动，因此它命名植物学家做什么，而不是他们是谁。

entries.definition: A person who studies living things. Botanist is a narrower kind of biologist, limited to plants.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物的人。botanist 是 biologist 中较窄的一类，限于植物。

entries.definition: A person who grows and cultivates plants for gardens, food, or sale. The focus is on producing plants, not on producing knowledge about them.
entries.definitionCN: 为园艺、食用或销售而栽培植物的人。重点在产出植株，而不是产出关于植物的知识。

entries.definition: A person who uses plants as medicine, often in a traditional practice. Botanist studies plants scientifically rather than treating patients with them.
entries.definitionCN: 用植物治病、常从事传统实践的人。botanist 以科学方式研究植物，而不是用植物治疗病人。

entries.definition: A person who studies how organisms relate to their environment. A botanist may study a plant's ecology, but the ecologist's unit is the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境关系的人。植物学家可能研究某种植物的生态，但生态学家的单位是整个系统。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the agent suffix -ist, the field noun botany, and the working verbs botanize and botanically describe.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：施动后缀 -ist、学科名词 botany，以及实际使用的动词 botanize 与副词 botanically。

normal.en: botany + -ist = botanist: the field first, the person second. The suffix adds 'one who practises', not 'plant'.
normal.cn: botany + -ist = botanist：先有学科，再有人。后缀添加的是“从事者”，不是“植物”。

normal.en: The -ist in botanist is the same -ist as in artist and scientist: a person who does the work.
normal.cn: botanist 里的 -ist 与 artist、scientist 里的 -ist 相同：做这项工作的人。

normal.en: A field botanist carries a press and a notebook; the specimen is the first document of the science.
normal.cn: 野外植物学家带着标本夹和记录本；标本是这门科学的第一份文档。

normal.en: A taxonomic botanist owns the Latin names: genus and species are the addresses that make a plant findable.
normal.cn: 分类植物学家掌管拉丁名：属与种是让植物可被找到的地址。

normal.en: Botanist is narrower than biologist because botan- names plants, while bio- names life in general.
normal.cn: botanist 比 biologist 窄，因为 botan- 命名植物，而 bio- 命名一般生命。

abstract.en: A person bent over a flower with a lens: the whole profession is the act of looking closely and writing down what is seen.
abstract.cn: 一个人俯身用放大镜看花：整个职业就是靠近观察并把所见写下来。

abstract.en: A herbarium sheet is a passport: the plant travels through time because someone signed it with a Latin name.
abstract.cn: 一份腊叶标本就是一本护照：因为有人在上面签了拉丁名，这株植物得以穿越时间。

abstract.en: The botanist stands between the wild plant and the written record, turning a living thing into a repeatable observation.
abstract.cn: 植物学家站在野生植物与书面记录之间，把一个活物变成可重复的观察。

examples.en: The botanist spent the morning pressing specimens for the herbarium.
examples.cn: 这位植物学家花了一上午为标本馆压制标本。

examples.en: A botanist and a horticulturist worked together to save the rare orchid.
examples.cn: 一位植物学家和一位园艺师合作拯救这种稀有兰花。

examples.en: As a botanist, she is careful to distinguish mosses from lichens.
examples.cn: 作为植物学家，她谨慎地把苔藓与地衣区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “博坦尼斯特”——博物（博）学家在园里蹲（tan）下，拿着放大镜研究植物 → botanist 植物学家

root: botan-（植物、牧草，希腊 botanē / botanikos，经中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 入英语）+ -ist（施动后缀，希腊 -istēs，经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste）；-ist 表示从业者，不表示植物。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of botanist all name the same person from different angles: a trained plant scientist, a field collector, a namer, a specialist, a historical herbalist, an applied worker, a keen amateur, and two boundary cases.
sensesIntro.cn: botanist 的九个义项从不同角度命名同一种人：受过训练的植物科学家、野外采集者、命名者、专门方向研究者、历史中的草药师、应用工作者、热心的业余爱好者，以及两个边界情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who looks closely at plants, collects them, and turns them into named records.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人靠近观察植物、采集它们，并把它们变成有名字的记录。

branches.en: CORE: the agent noun itself, 'one who practises botany'.
branches.cn: 核心：施动名词本身，即“从事植物学的人”。

branches.en: FIELD AND NAME: collecting outdoors and naming in the herbarium are the two oldest halves of the job.
branches.cn: 野外与命名：户外采集与标本馆命名，是这份工作最古老的两半。

branches.en: SPECIALTY AND APPLICATION: the same noun takes modifiers for the layer studied or the sector worked in.
branches.cn: 专门方向与应用：同一个名词接受修饰语，标明研究层次或工作行业。

branches.en: HISTORY AND EVERYDAY: the old herbalist role and the knowledgeable amateur both stretch the word beyond the licensed profession.
branches.cn: 历史与日常：旧时的草药师角色与懂行的业余爱好者，都把词义拉到执照职业之外。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: horticulturist produces plants, biologist studies all life; botanist sits between them.
branches.cn: 边界：horticulturist 产出植株，biologist 研究一切生命；botanist 位于两者之间。

intro.en: Botanist has one live suffix, -ist, on a borrowed Greek stem. The suffix is productive and can be added to other fields, while botan- stays fixed and supplies the plant meaning.
intro.cn: botanist 在借来的希腊词干上只有一个活后缀 -ist。这个后缀能产，可加在其他领域上；botan- 则固定不变，提供植物义。

latinIntro.en: The botan- stem is Greek, carried into English through Medieval Latin botanicus and French botanique. The agent suffix -ist also has a Latin stage, -ista, before it reached French and English.
latinIntro.cn: botan- 词干是希腊语，经中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 与法语 botanique 进入英语。施动后缀 -ist 也有拉丁阶段 -ista，之后才到法语和英语。

items.meaning: a person who studies plants; the shift is from a field to its practitioner
items.meaningCN: 研究植物的人；语义从学科转到从业者
items.example: The botanist recorded the plant's habitat and date.
items.exampleCN: 这位植物学家记录了该植物的生境与日期。

items.structure: botan- + -y (name of a field, on the model of astronomy)
items.meaning: the science of plants; the noun that supplies the profession's field
items.meaningCN: 植物学；为这一职业提供学科名的名词
items.example: Botany and zoology were once taught together as natural history.
items.exampleCN: 植物学与动物学曾作为博物学一起教授。

items.meaning: pertaining to plants; the shorter adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；较短的那个形容词
items.example: The botanic garden dates from the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这座植物园可追溯到 18 世纪。

items.meaning: relating to plants or botany; the default adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；植物学的；默认形容词
items.example: The botanical description notes the leaf's hairs and veins.
items.exampleCN: 植物学描述记录了叶片的毛被与叶脉。

items.example: Botanically, the tomato is a berry.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上说，番茄是一种浆果。

items.structure: botan- + -ize (to act in a particular way)
items.meaning: to collect or study plants in the field
items.meaningCN: 在野外采集或研究植物
items.example: They botanized the coastal dunes at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 他们在退潮时考察了海岸沙丘的植物。

items.meaning: a person who studies how a culture uses plants
items.meaningCN: 研究某一文化如何使用植物的人
items.example: An ethnobotanist documented the village's medicinal plants.
items.exampleCN: 一位民族植物学家记录了该村的药用植物。

items.meaning: a person who studies fossil plants
items.example: The paleobotanist identified a fern from the Jurassic.
items.exampleCN: 这位古植物学家鉴定出一株侏罗纪蕨类。

items.meaning: the activity of collecting or studying plants in the field
items.meaningCN: 野外采集或研究植物的活动
items.example: A morning of botanizing produced forty pressed specimens.
items.exampleCN: 一个上午的植物考察采得四十份压制标本。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to plants; the source of the English stem
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与植物有关的；英语词干的来源

latinEntries.meaning: agent suffix 'one who practises'; the ancestor of English -ist
latinEntries.meaningCN: 施动后缀“从事者”；英语 -ist 的前身

definition_zh: 植物学；（某地区的）植物志
definition_en: the scientific study of plants, or the plant life of a particular region
core_image: 一张压制的叶片标本旁，摆着写满学名的标签与一把镊子
scene: 标本室里，学生把压制好的叶片按科属排进柜子，标签上写满学名。 Modern botany began when plants were classified by their parts rather than by their uses.
sceneCN: 这里 botany 指「植物学」（第 1 个义项：研究植物的科学）；句意为当植物按自身构造而非用途被分类时，现代植物学便开始了。

pos.zh: 植物学；植物区系；植物学著作

senses.title: The science of plants
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies plants and their structure, growth and classification
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物及其结构、生长与分类的生物学分支
senses.example: Modern botany began with systematic classification.
senses.exampleCN: 现代植物学始于系统分类。
senses.why: the Greek root names herbage or fodder, so the science is literally the study of what grows as herb.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根指草料或饲草，因此这门科学字面上就是研究「长成草的东西」。

senses.title: The plant life of a region
senses.definition: all the plants growing in a particular area, considered as a group
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物，作为整体来看
senses.example: The island's botany is dominated by ferns and mosses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛的植物以蕨与苔藓为主。
senses.why: a discipline can lend its name to its subject matter, as geology names the rocks of a region.
senses.whyCN: 学科名可以借给它的研究对象，正如地质学也用来说一个地区的岩石。

senses.title: The subject as taught
senses.definition: the school or university subject in which plants are studied
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里研究植物的课程
senses.example: She took botany in her first year and never left the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她一年级修了植物学，从此没离开这个领域。
senses.why: the noun names the course because the course teaches the science, with no change of form.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名课程，因为课程所教的正是这门科学，词形没有变化。

senses.title: Economic botany
senses.titleCN: 经济植物学（把植物作为资源）
senses.definition: the study of plants as crops, medicines and raw materials
senses.definitionCN: 把植物作为作物、药材与原料来研究
senses.example: Economic botany traced the rubber plant from forest to factory.
senses.exampleCN: 经济植物学追溯橡胶植物从森林到工厂的路径。
senses.why: the field is defined by its use of plants, so an adjective narrows the general noun.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域以植物的用途来界定，因此用形容词收窄了通名。

senses.title: Field botany
senses.definition: the practical study of plants where they grow, chiefly by identifying them
senses.definitionCN: 在植物生长地进行的实务研究，主要是识别它们
senses.example: Field botany needs a hand lens and a great deal of patience.
senses.exampleCN: 野外植物学需要放大镜与极大的耐心。
senses.why: field marks the place of study, the opposite of laboratory botany.
senses.whyCN: 「野外」一词标记研究场所，与实验室植物学相对。

senses.title: Medical botany
senses.definition: the study of plants used as drugs or remedies
senses.definitionCN: 研究用作药物或疗法的植物
senses.example: Medical botany supplied most of the early pharmacopoeia.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的药典大多来自药用植物学。
senses.why: the adjective names the purpose, so the same science is practised for healing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词命名用途，同一门科学因此为治疗服务。

senses.title: A treatise or textbook of botany
senses.definition: a written work setting out the science of plants
senses.definitionCN: 系统阐述植物科学的著作
senses.example: He carried an old botany with him on every walk.
senses.exampleCN: 每次散步他都带着一本旧植物学书。
senses.why: a book is named after its subject, a common shorthand among sciences.
senses.whyCN: 书以主题命名，这是科学领域常见的简写。

senses.title: Systematic botany
senses.definition: the branch that names, describes and arranges plants into groups
senses.definitionCN: 命名、描述并把植物编入类群的分支
senses.example: Systematic botany still revises the family tree of flowering plants.
senses.exampleCN: 系统植物学仍在修订被子植物的谱系。
senses.why: systematic marks the classifying task, which is the oldest part of the science.
senses.whyCN: 「系统的」一词标记分类任务，而这门科学最古老的部分正是分类。

intro.en: Botany is the noun of botanic, from Latin botanicus and Greek botanikos 'of herbs', from botane 'grass, herb, fodder'. The deeper origin of botane is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: botany 是 botanic 的名词，后者来自拉丁 botanicus 与希腊 botanikos「草本的」，出自 botane「草、草本、饲草」。botane 的更早来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Botane meant 'grass, herb, pasture, fodder'; the science therefore began as the study of herbage rather than of all plants.
items.cn: botane 意为「草、草本、牧场、饲草」；这门科学因此起初是研究草料，而非一切植物。

items.en: Botanikos 'of herbs' was the adjective used for knowledge about plants and their uses.
items.cn: botanikos「草本的」是用于指植物及其用途知识的形容词。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as botanicus; the noun botanice followed in Medieval and Renaissance Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 botanicus；名词 botanice 随后出现在中世纪与文艺复兴拉丁语中。

items.en: English botany is recorded in the seventeenth century, when plant study separated from medicine and agriculture.
items.cn: 英语 botany 于 17 世纪有记录，当时植物研究从医学与农业中分离出来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of botane is unresolved; its link to boskein 'to feed' is generally accepted within Greek but the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：botane 在希腊语之前的来源没有定论；它与 boskein「喂养」的联系在希腊语内部一般被接受，但更深的词根属重构。

items.en: Source uncertain (coining date): the exact first appearance of botany in English print is not settled, so the seventeenth-century dating is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（造词年代）：botany 首次见于英语印刷的确切时间尚无定论，因此 17 世纪的系年只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates the botanic family by part of speech; group two separates the science from its neighbouring disciplines and from plant cover.
note.cn: 第一组按词类区分 botanic 词族；第二组区分这门科学与相邻学科及植物覆盖。

entries.definition: Relating to plants or to botany; the adjective describes, while botany names the field.
entries.definitionCN: 与植物或植物学有关；形容词起描述作用，botany 命名领域。

entries.definition: A person who studies plants, formed with -ist; the field is botany, the practitioner is a botanist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的人，由 -ist 构成；领域是 botany，从业者是 botanist。

entries.definition: To collect and study plants in the field; it is the verb, not the science.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外采集并研究植物；是动词，而非学科名。

entries.definition: The older adjective form, still used in names such as botanic garden; it is not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的形容词形式，仍见于「植物园」等名称；它不是名词。

entries.definition: The study of all living things; botany is the plant branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切生物的科学；botany 是其中研究植物的分支。

entries.definition: The practice of growing garden plants; it applies botanical knowledge rather than producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 栽培园林植物的实务；它应用植物学知识，而非生产知识。

entries.definition: The plant species of a region or period, usually listed systematically; botany can also name the study of that list.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区或某时期的植物物种，通常系统列出；botany 也可指对这份名录的研究。

entries.definition: Plants as ground cover, described by structure rather than by species; it is what botany studies, not the study.
entries.definitionCN: 作为地面覆盖的植物，按结构而非物种描述；它是植物学的研究对象，而非这门学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real academic phrases and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的学术搭配与真实词族。

normal.en: botane 'herb' + -y: the study of herbs, now of all plants.
normal.cn: botane「草本」+ -y：研究草本之学，如今研究一切植物。

normal.en: The family splits by word class: botany, botanic, botanical, botanist.
normal.cn: 词族按词类分开：botany、botanic、botanical、botanist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field botany, economic botany, medical botany.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外植物学、经济植物学、药用植物学。

normal.en: The subject also names the plants of a place: the botany of an island.
normal.cn: 学科名也指一地植物：某岛的植物志。

normal.en: Its neighbour is zoology; together they were natural history.
normal.cn: 它的邻居是动物学；二者合起来曾是自然史。

abstract.en: Picture a pressed leaf beside a label written in careful Latin.
abstract.cn: 想象一片压制的叶子，旁边是工整拉丁文的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a walk that turns into a survey because every plant gets a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一次散步变成调查，因为每株植物都被取了名。

abstract.en: Picture a library where the shelves are organised by family rather than by use.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架按科属而非用途排列。

examples.en: Botany and zoology were once taught together as natural history.
examples.cn: 植物学与动物学曾作为自然史一起教授。

examples.en: The botany of the delta includes more than four hundred species.
examples.cn: 这片三角洲的植物超过四百种。

examples.en: Economic botany studies how plants become food, fibre and medicine.
examples.cn: 经济植物学研究植物如何变成食物、纤维与药物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「botan（草）+ y」——研究草与植物的学问 → 植物学

root: 希腊 botane「草、草本、饲草」→ botanikos「草本的」→ 拉丁 botanicus → 英语 botany。botane 的更早来源不确定，与 boskein「喂养」的联系在希腊语内部一般被接受。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of botany move from the science itself to the plants it studies, the course that teaches it, its applied branches and the book that records it.
sensesIntro.cn: botany 的八个义项从这门科学本身，移向它所研究的植物、教授它的课程、它的应用分支，以及记录它的书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pressed leaf and a label written in Latin, side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片压制的叶子与一张拉丁文标签并排放着。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND SUBJECT MATTER: the discipline lends its name to the plants it studies.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：学科名借给它所研究的植物。

branches.en: TAUGHT AND WRITTEN: a course and a book both carry the name of the science.
branches.cn: 教与写：课程与书都以这门科学命名。

branches.en: APPLIED BRANCHES: crops and medicines narrow the field by purpose.
branches.cn: 应用分支：作物与药材按用途收窄领域。

branches.en: THE FIELD: identification outdoors is the oldest practical skill.
branches.cn: 野外：户外识别是最古老的实务技能。

branches.en: THE ORDER: naming and grouping is the backbone of the science.
branches.cn: 秩序：命名与归群是这门科学的骨干。

intro.en: Botany is a Greek adjective turned into an English noun, and its family names the field, the practitioner and the activity.
intro.cn: botany 是希腊形容词转成的英语名词，其词族命名领域、从业者与活动。

latinIntro.en: Greek botane 'herb' gives botanikos and Latin botanicus; English botany, botanic, botanical and botanist all descend from that adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 botane「草本」衍生 botanikos 与拉丁 botanicus；英语的 botany、botanic、botanical 与 botanist 都出自那个形容词。

items.example: The root names what grows as herb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名长成草的东西。

items.example: Botany names the study of plants.
items.exampleCN: botany 命名研究植物的学问。

items.example: The botanic garden holds living collections.

items.exampleCN: 植物学名遵循国际规则。

items.example: The botanist keyed out the unknown sedge.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家检索出了那种未知的莎草。

items.meaning: to collect plants in the field
items.example: They botanized the ridge before the road went in.
items.exampleCN: 在修路之前，他们在山脊采集植物。

items.meaning: the study of people's use of plants
items.example: Ethnobotany records which plants a village uses for medicine.
items.exampleCN: 民族植物学记录一个村庄用哪些植物做药。

items.example: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上看，番茄是果实。

definition_zh: 打扰；费心；麻烦事
definition_en: to disturb or annoy someone
core_image: 轻轻敲门、怕惊动别人的人
scene: 他轻轻敲门，不想打扰正在工作的人。He knocked softly so as not to bother anyone.
sceneCN: 这里 bother 是「打扰」（第 1 个义项：给人添麻烦、使人分心）；句意是他轻轻敲门，以免打扰别人。

pos.zh: 名词：麻烦，令人烦恼的事

senses.title: To disturb someone
senses.definition: to interrupt or trouble someone
senses.definitionCN: 打断或给别人添麻烦
senses.example: He knocked softly so as not to bother anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻轻敲门，以免打扰别人。
senses.why: This is the main sense, from a word for confusing or worrying.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要义项，来自表示使人困惑或担忧的词。

senses.title: To make an effort
senses.definition: to take the trouble to do something
senses.definitionCN: 不嫌麻烦地去做某事
senses.example: Don't bother cooking for me.
senses.exampleCN: 不用为我费心做饭了。
senses.why: If an act is a trouble, then bothering is making that effort.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事是麻烦，那么 bother 就是付出这份心力。

senses.title: A small trouble
senses.definition: a small problem or an annoying effort
senses.definitionCN: 小问题或令人烦恼的麻烦
senses.example: The delay was a bit of a bother.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误有点麻烦。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the trouble itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，指麻烦本身。

intro.en: Bother appeared in the eighteenth century, and its origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: bother 出现于十八世纪，来源不明。

items.en: bother appeared in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: bother 出现于十八世纪。

items.en: bother meant to confuse or worry.
items.cn: bother 意为使人困惑或担忧。

items.en: bother named a small trouble.
items.cn: bother 指小小的麻烦。

items.en: don't bother became a polite refusal.
items.cn: don't bother 成为礼貌的拒绝。

items.en: bother covers disturbing, effort and trouble.
items.cn: 如今 bother 兼指打扰、费心与麻烦。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by letters; the near-meaning group names disturbing and annoying.
note.cn: 形近组字母相近；近义组是打扰与使人生气。

the line between two countries
to cause difficulty for someone
to interrupt someone

normalIntro.en: Bother is a small knock at a bad time, and the effort you would rather not make.
normalIntro.cn: bother 是不合时宜的一声敲门，也是你不愿花的那份力气。

normal.en: Bother and bothered are the base and past forms.
normal.cn: 原形是 bother，过去式是 bothered。

normal.en: Sorry to bother you is a polite opening.

definition_zh: adj. 麻烦的，令人烦恼的
definition_en: causing annoyance, especially through small repeated irritations rather than real difficulty

definition_zh: n. 巨石，大圆石；（地质）巨砾

core_image: 冰川退去后，田中央留下的一块圆石

senses.exampleCN: 他连续几个星期吹嘘自己的新车。
senses.why: The core image is the swollen voice: pride forcing itself out of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是膨胀的声音：骄傲从嘴里挤出来。

senses.title: To boast before proving
senses.definition: to claim victory or ability in advance of the result
senses.definitionCN: 在结果出来之前宣称必胜或自称有能
senses.example: They bragged they would finish the job by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夸口周五之前就能完工。
senses.why: Swollen talk runs ahead of swollen deeds, so claiming comes before doing.
senses.whyCN: 嘴上的膨胀跑在行动前面，宣称便先于做成。

senses.title: To speak boastfully on someone's behalf
senses.definition: to praise another, often one's own family, in a boastful way
senses.definitionCN: 以夸口的口吻称赞他人，常指家人
senses.example: Grandmother brags of her grandchildren endlessly.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母没完没了地夸自己的孙辈。
senses.why: One's own pride extends naturally to what belongs to one's own circle.
senses.whyCN: 对自身的骄傲自然延伸到自己圈内的人和物。

senses.title: A boastful statement
senses.definition: an instance of boasting; a thing said with too much pride
senses.definitionCN: 一次吹嘘；说得过头的话
senses.example: That was no brag; he really did it.
senses.exampleCN: 那不是大话；他真的做到了。
senses.why: The act names its product, as talk leaves words behind.
senses.whyCN: 行为命名其产物，正如言谈留下话语。

senses.title: A proud claim worth making
senses.definition: something to be proud of, as in bragging rights
senses.definitionCN: 足以自豪之事，如 bragging rights（夸耀的资本）
senses.example: Winning the league gave them bragging rights for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得联赛让他们有一年的夸耀资本。
senses.why: Since boasting implies grounds, the grounds themselves take the word's name.
senses.whyCN: 吹嘘必有凭据，凭据便借用了这个词的名字。

senses.title: First-rate, of the best kind
senses.definition: outstanding or first-rate, in older or dialect use
senses.definitionCN: 卓越的、一流的，见于旧用法或方言
senses.example: In old use, a brag horse meant the finest horse.
senses.exampleCN: 旧用法中 brag horse 指最好的马。
senses.why: Boastful excess shades into superlative praise of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 夸口的过分反转为对事物本身的最高级称赞。

senses.title: A card game of bluffing
senses.definition: a British card game in which bluffing is central, ancestor of poker
senses.definitionCN: 一种以虚张声势为核心的英国纸牌游戏，扑克的祖先
senses.example: The sailors passed the night playing brag.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们打了一夜的吹牛纸牌。
senses.why: The game is named for its chief move: talking up a weak hand.
senses.whyCN: 该游戏因其核心动作得名：把弱牌吹成强牌。

senses.title: A loud or startling sound or thing
senses.definition: in older use, a thunderous noise or a striking thing
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指雷鸣般的响声或令人吃惊的事物
senses.example: Early texts used brag for a burst of thunder.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文本用 brag 指一声炸雷。
senses.why: The swollen voice began as swollen sound before it became swollen words.
senses.whyCN: 膨胀之声先于膨胀之词，词义由响声起家。

intro.en: Brag arose in Middle English, probably imitative of loud talk, with possible Norse connections; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: brag 产生于中古英语，一般认为是对大声说话的拟声，或与诺斯语有关；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse braka meant to creak or crack; a link is generally suggested but not proven.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 braka 意为吱嘎作响、爆裂；一般认为有关联但未获证实。

items.en: Brag first meant to make a loud noise, then to talk loudly and proudly.
items.cn: 十四世纪 brag 先指发出巨响，后指大声而骄傲地说话。

items.en: The adjective brag meant spirited or first-rate, as in brag lines of verse.
items.cn: 形容词 brag 意为神气的、一流的，见于诗行描写。

items.en: The noun and the card game name appear; Shakespeare uses brag both as noun and adjective.
items.cn: 十六世纪出现名词用法及纸牌戏名；莎翁笔下 brag 兼作名词与形容词。

items.en: Derivatives braggart, braggadocio (coined in Spenser), and bragging rights spread.
items.cn: 派生词 braggart、braggadocio（斯宾塞所创）与 bragging rights 流行开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb, noun, and the phrase bragging rights; the adjective is archaic.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词、名词与 bragging rights 短语；形容词义已属古旧。

note.en: Brag heads a noisy family of boast words; its sound twins bray and brace are unrelated.
note.cn: brag 是一片吹嘘之词的源头；音近的 bray、brace 与之无关。

normalIntro.cn: brass 是乐队里听得到的明亮金属。

normal.en: A brass band marched past.
normal.cn: 一支铜管乐队走过。

normal.en: Brass buttons shine after polishing.
normal.cn: 黄铜纽扣擦过就发亮。

normal.en: The top brass joined the meeting.
normal.cn: 高层参加了会议。

normal.en: Brass has no plural in this sense.
normal.cn: 这个义项里 brass 没有复数。

normal.en: Copper and zinc make brass.
normal.cn: 铜与锌合成黄铜。

abstract.en: See a polished horn under stage lights.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台灯下擦亮的铜号。

abstract.en: See yellow buttons on a uniform.
abstract.cn: 想象制服上的黄色纽扣。

abstract.en: See a row of senior officers at a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一桌高级官员。

examples.en: The brass shone under the lights of the band.
examples.cn: 乐队的铜管在灯下发亮。

examples.en: The brass came in after the drums.
examples.cn: 鼓声之后铜管声部进来了。

examples.en: The top brass met behind closed doors.
examples.cn: 高层在闭门会议中碰面。

dict_mnemonic.text: brass 里有 ass，驴子驮着黄铜，阳光一照金灿灿，记住它是黄铜。

root: brass 源自古英语 bræs，指铜锌合成的黄色金属，十六世纪起指用这种金属做的乐器，十九世纪又用 top brass 指高级军官，引申为机构高层。

sensesIntro.en: A yellow metal, the instruments made from it and the people at the top.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种黄色金属、用它制成的乐器、站在顶层的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polished yellow horn under stage lights.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台灯下擦得发亮的黄色铜号。

intro.en: Brass forms adjectives and nouns with -y and -ware.
intro.cn: brass 加 -y 与 -ware 构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old English; the Latin items below are related only in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。
